Consult Summary:
- Adult female presented via teleconsult with acute continuous vertigo (room-spinning) for ~2 hours with nausea, unsteady gait, and bilateral ear buzzing; no focal neurologic deficits, no ear pain or discharge, no recent viral illness; clinician impression: likely labyrinthitis; symptomatic medication prescribed (name not captured) and in-person evaluation arranged with emergency precautions advised.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dizziness described as room-spinning vertigo, onset ~2 hours prior while making breakfast; continuous since onset. Associated nausea, unsteady gait (able to walk but not straight), and ear buzzing.
- Prior episode: Similar brief episode ~1 month ago lasting 5–10 minutes that resolved quickly.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea; tinnitus (“buzzing” in ears).
- Pertinent negatives: No vomiting to date, no ear pain, no ear discharge, no hearing loss, no fever reported, no recent cough/cold or viral illness, no weakness of arms/legs.
- Functional impact: Feels unstable due to spinning sensation; extremity strength reported intact.

Past Medical History:
- Premature ovarian failure; on hormone replacement therapy (HRT). 
- Conflict noted: Clinician stated “premature hearing failure” during documentation, which conflicts with patient’s report of “premature ovarian failure.”

Medications:
- HRT (hormone replacement therapy) for premature ovarian failure; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New prescription: Medication name not documented (inaudible). Instructions: 1 tablet three times daily for 10 days; can be taken with or without food; dose/strength and route not documented.
- Allergies: No known allergies.

Social History:
- Mentions husband (was preparing breakfast). No additional social, tobacco, alcohol, or substance history documented.

Family History:
- Not mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- None completed during teleconsult.
- Plan for in-person assessment: Ear examination, blood pressure check, and assessment of gait/neurologic function.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute vertigo, likely peripheral etiology (labyrinthitis per clinician impression).
  - Start symptomatic medication (name not captured): 1 tablet TID for 10 days; may take with or without food.
  - Arrange in-person appointment in the next few days for otoscopic exam, blood pressure measurement, and evaluation of gait/neurologic status.
  - Safety-netting: Seek urgent care/A&E if new weakness of arms/legs, sudden severe headache, or persistent/violent vomiting occurs.
  - Prescription to be sent to Lloyds Pharmacy per system record.
- Issue 2: Nausea associated with vertigo.
  - Managed with the above symptomatic treatment; no separate antiemetic documented.

- General Plan items:
  - Patient instructed to contact support to book the in-person appointment.
  - Continue monitoring symptoms; further management to follow in-person evaluation findings.

Quality checks:
- Missing typical elements: Vitals, full neurological exam (including nystagmus, cerebellar testing), orthostatic blood pressure, hearing assessment, complete medication list reconciliation, full allergy clarification (drug vs. non-drug), social history (tobacco/alcohol/substances), family history.
- Internal conflicts: “Premature ovarian failure” reported by patient vs. clinician mention of “premature hearing failure” (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: One medication name was inaudible/omitted; otherwise clear history with minor phrasing ambiguities.
